title: BanzaCleanRoomQuestionLedgerEntry
description: One question raised by an implementer working from a clean-room export package. The ledger is EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE, not norm: it records what an external reader could not determine from the published surface, so that gaps are measured rather than guessed at. Nothing in a ledger entry imposes a requirement on anyone, and no entry may be cited as a rule.
_authority: This schema constrains the ledger's shape. The ledger records observations; the Normative Manifest remains the authority on what BANZA requires. A ledger entry can cause a normative change — it can never be one.

trial_id.description: Which trial raised it. Questions from different trials are not comparable as a single population: a second team reading the same package after the first has reported gaps is not an independent observation.

timestamp.description: When the question was raised. Ordering matters here — a question raised in the first hour and one raised on the third day are different evidence about discoverability.

external_profile_id.description: Required when target_profile is L4: L4 is parameterized, and 'L4' alone does not identify an evaluation configuration.

package_digest.description: SHA-256 of the package manifest the implementer was working from. A question is only interpretable against the exact material that produced it.

artefact.description: The file the question is about, as a path inside the package. `none` where the question is about something the package does not contain — which is itself the most interesting kind of entry.

location.description: Where in that artefact: a section, a member, a vector id. Free text, because the artefacts do not share one addressing scheme.

question.description: The question as the implementer asked it. Recorded verbatim: rewriting it into what we think they meant destroys the evidence.

classification.description: See clean-room/README.md for what each means. The set is closed: a question that seems to need a new category is a finding about the categories, to be argued before the set changes, not during a trial.

classification_note.description: Why this classification and not a neighbouring one. Required in practice for MISSING_RULE and CONFLICT, which assert a defect in the surface.

resolution.description: What answered it, or that it is still open. An answer that had to come from a person is a different result from one found in the package, and the text should say which.

answered_from_package_alone.description: Whether the implementer could resolve it from the package without asking anyone. This is the measurement the trial exists to take.

normative_change_required.description: Whether answering it required changing the normative surface. True here is the strongest possible finding: the specification was incomplete or wrong.

resolved_by_commit.description: The commit that made the change, where normative_change_required is true.

caused_by_vector_grammar.description: Whether this question exists because the vector files state expected outcomes in different shapes. Recorded to measure a known open item without prompting anyone to complain about it; implementers are not told this field exists.
